messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
在大氣壓（101.3 kPa）下，純水的凝固點是 0 °C。  
冰–水相變曲線的斜率約為 \(dT/dP \approx +9.5\) K / MPa（即每增加 1 MPa 壓力，凝固點上升約 9.5 K）。  

將此斜率用於 10 kPa 的條件：

\[
\Delta P = 10\,\text{kPa} - 101.3\,\text{kPa} = -91.3\,\text{kPa}
= -0.0913\,\text{MPa}
\]

\[
\Delta T = dT/dP \times \Delta P \approx 9.5\,\frac{\text{K}}{\text{MPa}}\times(-0.0913\,\text{MPa})
\approx -0.87\,\text{K}
\]

因此，在 10 kPa 時，水的凝固點大約是：

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \approx 0\,^\circ\text{C} - 0.87\,^\circ\text{C}
\approx -0.9\,^\circ\text{C}
\]

**答案：** 約 **−0.9 °C**（四捨五入到小數點後一位）。
message.reasoning: The user asks: "在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？" They want the freezing point of water at 10 kPa. The tool calculates boiling point, not freezing point. There's no direct tool for freezing point. We can approximate using known relation: freezing point depression? But at low pressure, water may boil before freezing. At 10 kPa (~0.1 atm), water boils at ~45°C? Actually boiling point at 100 kPa is 100°C; at 10 kPa it's about 45°C. Freezing point at 10 kPa might be lower than 0°C? For pure water, freezing point decreases with decreasing pressure? Actually freezing point of water increases slightly as pressure decreases? Wait, water has negative slope of melting curve: at higher pressure, freezing point decreases (like ice melts under pressure). So at lower pressure, freezing point increases? Let's recall: Ice Ih melting line has positive slope? Actually the melting curve of ice I has a negative slope? Let's check: The Clapeyron equation: dP/dT = ΔS/ΔV. For ice-water transition, ΔV = V_liquid - V_ice > 0 (liquid volume larger). ΔS = S_liquid - S_ice > 0. So dP/dT = ΔS/ΔV > 0. So melting temperature increases with pressure. So at lower pressure, melting temperature decreases. So at 10 kPa, freezing point will be below 0°C. How much? The melting curve near 0°C: dT/dP = ΔV/ΔS. For ice Ih, slope ~ 9.5 K/MPa? Actually typical slope ~ 9.5 K/MPa. So at 90 kPa difference from 101.3 kPa, change ~ 0.09 MPa * 9.5 K/MPa = 0.855 K. So at 10 kPa, difference from 101.3 kPa is 91.3 kPa = 0.0913 MPa. Multiply by 9.5 K/MPa gives ~0.867 K. So freezing point at 10 kPa would be ~0°C - 0.867K = -0.867°C. Roughly -0.87°C. But we need to provide answer. There's no tool. So we can respond with approximate value. Use knowledge. Provide explanation.
